title: Deion Sanders
description: American football coach and former player (born 1967)
wiki_lead:
Deion Luwynn Sanders Sr. (born August 9, 1967) is an American football coach and former player who is the head football coach at the University of Colorado Boulder. Nicknamed "Prime Time" and "Coach Prime", he played in the National Football League (NFL) for 14 seasons with the Atlanta Falcons, San Francisco 49ers, Dallas Cowboys, Washington Redskins, and Baltimore Ravens. Sanders was also a baseball outfielder for nine seasons in Major League Baseball (MLB) with the New York Yankees, Atlanta Braves, Cincinnati Reds, and San Francisco Giants. He won two Super Bowl titles and made one World Series appearance in 1992, making him the only athlete in history to play in both a Super Bowl and a World Series.
Sanders played college football for the Florida State Seminoles, winning the Jim Thorpe Award in 1988. He was selected by the Falcons fifth overall in the 1989 NFL draft. Primarily a cornerback, he received eight Pro Bowl and six first-team All-Pro selections. Sanders also made consecutive Super Bowl appearances in Super Bowl XXIX with the 49ers and Super Bowl XXX with the Cowboys, winning both. He was inducted to the Pro Football Hall of Fame and the College Football Hall of Fame in 2011.
After retiring as a player, Sanders pursued a sports analyst and coaching career. He served as the head coach at Jackson State University from 2020 to 2022, leading them to two consecutive Celebration Bowl appearances and the first undefeated regular season in school history. Sanders was named the head football coach of Colorado in 2023. He has gained publicity for the university and its football program, though the team's on-field success has been limited.

Early life
Sanders was born on August 9, 1967, in Fort Myers, Florida, to Connie Sanders and Mims Sanders. His parents divorced when Sanders was two years old. Sanders was raised by his mother and her new husband, Willie Knight, whom Sanders credits with being influential in his life. He attended North Fort Myers High School, and was a letterman and All-State honoree in football, basketball and baseball. In 1985, Sanders was named to the Florida High School Association All-Century Team which selected the top 33 players in the 100-year history of high school football in the state.
The Kansas City Royals selected Sanders out of North Fort Myers High School in the sixth round of the 1985 Major League Baseball draft. Sanders decided to play with Florida State University instead of signing with the Kansas City Royals.
On the New Heights podcast, Sanders revealed his first name is spelled "Dion" but he started spelling it "Deion" when learning the nursery rhyme "Old MacDonald Had a Farm" as a child.


College career

Sanders enrolled at Florida State University and played three sports for the Florida State Seminoles: football, baseball, and track. grok_lead: Deion Sanders (born August 9, 1967) is an American former professional football and baseball player, television personality, and college football coach, best known for his exceptional athletic versatility and nicknamed "Prime Time" for his flamboyant style and on-field dominance. He is the only athlete in history to appear in both a Super Bowl and a World Series, achieving this career feat with a World Series appearance in 1992 while playing in the NFL regular season for the Atlanta Falcons and participating in MLB playoffs with the Atlanta Braves. Sanders excelled as a cornerback and return specialist in the NFL over a 14-season career from 1989 to 2005, playing for the Atlanta Falcons, San Francisco 49ers, Dallas Cowboys, Washington Redskins, and Baltimore Ravens, where he recorded 53 interceptions, 1,331 interception return yards (second all-time at retirement), and an NFL-record 19 total return touchdowns. Selected fifth overall in the 1989 NFL Draft after a standout college career at Florida State University âwhere he earned two-time All-American honors, the 1988 Jim Thorpe Award as the nation's top defensive back, and set school records with 14 interceptionsâhe won two Super Bowls (XXIX with the 49ers in 1994 and XXX with the Cowboys in 1995), was named NFL Defensive Player of the Year in 1994, earned eight Pro Bowl selections, and six First-Team All-Pro honors before his induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2011. In baseball, Sanders played nine MLB seasons from 1989 to 2001 as an outfielder for the New York Yankees, Atlanta Braves, Cincinnati Reds, and San Francisco Giants, compiling a.263 batting average, 39 home runs, 168 RBIs, 186 stolen bases, and a 5.5 Wins Above Replacement value, with his speed and defense highlighting his contributions during overlapping football seasons. Transitioning to coaching after retiring as a player, Sanders served as head coach at Jackson State University from 2020 to 2022, where he compiled a 27-6 record, won two Southwestern Athletic Conference (SWAC) championships, and earned the 2021 Eddie Robinson Award as the top Football Championship Subdivision (FCS) coach, leading the Tigers to a 16-0 SWAC regular season record over his final two seasons. In December 2022, he became head coach of the Colorado Buffaloes, revitalizing the program from a 1-11 record in 2022; his teams achieved a 4-8 mark in 2023, a 9-4 finish with a bowl berth in 2024, and a 3-7 record as of November 19, 2025, yielding an overall 16-19 record at Colorado amid high-profile recruiting and national attention.
